common_name: Designer Threads Creamy Calico Threadleaf Coreopsis (Maroon-Eyed Soft Yellow Tickseed)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Creamy Calico is a patented (USPP 36,035) Proven Winners Designer Threads threadleaf coreopsis selected for a sharply bicolor flower pattern.

directions: Creamy Calico produces soft yellow flowers each stamped with a broad, well-defined deep maroon eye zone, a bolder bicolor pattern than most threadleaf coreopsis, held above fine, airy, needle-like foliage through summer. It forms a dense mound wider than it is tall and tolerates heat and drought well once established in average, well-drained soil in full sun. Shear plants back lightly after the first flush to encourage rebloom and keep the habit tidy. It attracts bees and butterflies while resisting deer browsing.
sources: Proven Winners plant profile — Designer Threads Creamy Calico Coreopsis verticillata, USPP 36,035 (provenwinners.com/plants/coreopsis)

common_name: Designer Threads Golden Needles Threadleaf Coreopsis (Mildew-Resistant Maroon-Eyed Golden Tickseed)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Golden Needles is a patented (USPP 36,034) Designer Threads selection chosen specifically for exceptional mildew resistance.

directions: Golden Needles bears golden yellow flowers with sharply defined maroon central eye zones over fine, thread-like foliage, and the breeder singles it out within the Designer Threads line for exceptional resistance to powdery mildew. That trait makes it a good choice for humid climates where older threadleaf coreopsis selections typically decline by late summer. Grow it in average, well-drained soil in full sun; it tolerates drought once established and needs little more than an occasional post-bloom shearing to stay neat. Bees and butterflies visit the flowers freely, while deer generally leave it alone.
sources: Proven Winners plant profile — Designer Threads Golden Needles Coreopsis verticillata, USPP 36,034 (provenwinners.com/plants/coreopsis)

common_name: Designer Threads Heartstrings Threadleaf Coreopsis (Cream Tickseed with Reddish-Pink Eye)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Heartstrings is a patented (USPP 36,055) Designer Threads selection with an unusually soft cream-and-pink color combination for this species.

directions: Heartstrings opens pale cream flowers centered on a dark reddish-pink eye, a softer, warmer color combination than the yellow-dominant shades typical of threadleaf coreopsis, carried over the same fine, airy, needle-like foliage as its series-mates. It forms a dense, mounding clump and blooms through summer in average, well-drained soil and full sun, tolerating heat and drought once established. Light shearing after the first bloom flush encourages a tidy rebound of new growth and flowers. Like other Designer Threads selections it draws bees and butterflies and resists deer.
sources: Proven Winners plant profile — Designer Threads Heartstrings Coreopsis verticillata, USPP 36,055 (provenwinners.com/plants/coreopsis)

common_name: Designer Threads Scarlet Ribbons Threadleaf Coreopsis (Solid Velvety Maroon-Red Tickseed)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Scarlet Ribbons is a patented (USPP 35,961) Designer Threads selection notable for solid, unmarked petal color rather than the bicolor eye pattern typical of the genus.

directions: Scarlet Ribbons stands apart within its series and the wider genus for petals that are a velvety, solid maroon-red from base to tip rather than the contrasting-eye bicolor pattern seen on most threadleaf coreopsis, held over fine, thread-like foliage. The compact, dense habit makes it useful toward the front of a border or in mass plantings where a saturated, uniform flower color reads strongly from a distance. Grow it in average, well-drained soil in full sun; once established it tolerates drought well and benefits from a light shearing after its first flush to prompt rebloom. Bees and butterflies visit readily, and deer tend to avoid it.
sources: Proven Winners plant profile — Designer Threads Scarlet Ribbons Coreopsis verticillata, USPP 35,961 (provenwinners.com/plants/coreopsis)

common_name: Cherry Pie Coreopsis (Compact Cherry-Red Annual Tickseed)

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants after all frost danger has passed in well-drained, average soil in full sun; Cherry Pie is a patented (USPP 22,479) low, spreading annual coreopsis bred as a container filler.

directions: Cherry Pie forms a low, spreading mound smothered in cherry-red flowers from summer through fall, making it a distinctive filler for mixed containers and landscape edges rather than a typical upright tickseed. It performs well in heat and tolerates dry spells between waterings once roots are established in well-drained soil and full sun. As a vegetatively propagated patented selection it is reliably uniform from batch to batch, unlike seed-grown coreopsis, and only overwinters outdoors in the warmest zones. Butterflies visit the flowers steadily through its long bloom season.
sources: Proven Winners plant profile — Cherry Pie Coreopsis, USPP 22,479 (provenwinners.com/plants/coreopsis)

common_name: Pumpkin Pie Coreopsis (Compact Orange Annual Tickseed)

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants after all frost danger has passed in well-drained, average soil in full sun; Pumpkin Pie is a patented (USPP 22,519) low, spreading annual coreopsis bred as a container filler.

directions: Pumpkin Pie bears a continuous flush of orange flowers over a low, mounded, spreading habit, giving mixed containers and landscape plantings a warm filler color that most seed-grown tickseed selections don't offer. It is drought-tolerant once established and holds up well through summer heat in well-drained soil and full sun. Being a vegetatively propagated patented cultivar, plants are uniform and true-to-type, unlike open-pollinated coreopsis grown from seed. Butterflies are frequent visitors through its long summer-to-fall bloom period.
sources: Proven Winners plant profile — Pumpkin Pie Coreopsis, USPP 22,519 (provenwinners.com/plants/coreopsis)

common_name: Coloropsis Salsa Tickseed (Compact Upright Yellow-Flowered Coreopsis)

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants after all frost danger has passed in well-drained, average soil in full sun; Salsa is a patented (USPP 22,129) Coloropsis-series annual coreopsis with an unusually upright, non-spreading habit.

directions: Salsa grows into a narrow, upright mound of yellow flowers, a taller and considerably less spreading habit than most annual coreopsis bred for container fillers, making it useful as a thriller or mid-height accent instead. It is drought-tolerant and deer-resistant once established, holding its shape through summer heat in well-drained, average soil and full sun. As a patented, vegetatively propagated selection it performs consistently from plant to plant across a growing season. Flowers appear continuously from summer through fall and draw pollinating insects steadily.
sources: Proven Winners plant profile — Coloropsis Salsa Coreopsis, USPP 22,129 (provenwinners.com/plants/coreopsis)

common_name: Sunbeckia Carolina Black-Eyed Susan (Compact Large-Flowered Annual Rudbeckia)

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants after all frost danger has passed in well-drained, average soil in full sun; Sunbeckia Carolina is a compact Proven Selections black-eyed Susan bred for large flower size and long-lasting bloom.

directions: Sunbeckia Carolina grows into a compact, upright mound covered in large, long-lasting yellow black-eyed Susan flowers, one of three closely related Sunbeckia series selections bred for uniform habit and easy maintenance in containers and landscape mass plantings. Its even branching and reliable bloom size come from vegetative propagation rather than seed, giving consistent plants across a planting. Grow it in well-drained, average soil in full sun with average moisture; it needs little deadheading to keep flowering from summer through fall. Bees visit the flowers heavily throughout the bloom season.
sources: Proven Winners plant profile — Sunbeckia Carolina Rudbeckia hirta (provenwinners.com/plants/rudbeckia)

common_name: Sunbeckia Luna Black-Eyed Susan (Compact Large-Flowered Annual Rudbeckia)

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants after all frost danger has passed in well-drained, average soil in full sun; Sunbeckia Luna is a compact Proven Selections black-eyed Susan bred for large flower size and long-lasting bloom.

directions: Sunbeckia Luna forms the same compact, upright, well-branched mound as its Sunbeckia series-mates, bearing large yellow black-eyed Susan flowers over an extended summer-to-fall bloom window. Being vegetatively propagated rather than grown from seed, it offers a uniform habit and flower size that seed-grown hirta strains can't guarantee. Site it in well-drained, average soil in full sun with average watering; it holds up well in containers, landscape beds, and mass plantings with minimal grooming. Bees are frequent visitors throughout its long bloom period.
sources: Proven Winners plant profile — Sunbeckia Luna Rudbeckia hirta (provenwinners.com/plants/rudbeckia)

common_name: Sunbeckia Paulina Black-Eyed Susan (Compact Large-Flowered Annual Rudbeckia)

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants after all frost danger has passed in well-drained, average soil in full sun; Sunbeckia Paulina is a compact Proven Selections black-eyed Susan bred for large flower size and long-lasting bloom.

directions: Sunbeckia Paulina rounds out the Sunbeckia series with the same dense, compact, upright habit and large yellow black-eyed Susan flowers as its two series-mates, blooming heavily from summer through fall. As a vegetatively propagated selection it delivers consistent flower size and plant form, an advantage over variable seed-grown hirta strains for landscapers wanting uniform mass plantings. Grow it in well-drained, average soil in full sun with average moisture and minimal deadheading. It attracts bees steadily and performs well in containers as well as garden beds.
sources: Proven Winners plant profile — Sunbeckia Paulina Rudbeckia hirta (provenwinners.com/plants/rudbeckia)

common_name: Suntacular Black-Eyed Susan (Tall Columnar Bronze-Eyed Perennial Rudbeckia)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, average soil in full sun; Suntacular (breeder code NCRH2) is a patent-pending hybrid Rudbeckia bred for an unusually tall, narrow, columnar habit.

directions: Suntacular grows into a tall, narrow, columnar form the breeder describes as unlike the typical sprawling habit of most Rudbeckia, topped through summer with yellow flowers set off by a bronze-orange eye zone. The upright, self-supporting stems make it useful as a vertical accent toward the back of a border without the staking many tall perennials need. It is noted for disease resistance and deer resistance, performing well in well-drained, average soil in full sun with low supplemental water once established. It suits both container plantings and in-ground landscape use.
sources: Proven Winners plant profile — Suntacular Rudbeckia hybrid, breeder code NCRH2 USPPAF (provenwinners.com/plants/rudbeckia)
